picks.title: Google built a portable AI translator that works offline, and you can build one too
picks.excerpt: Google engineers ran Gemma 4 E4B on a Raspberry Pi inside a 3D-printed housing to make a fully offline AI translator. It is a working reference for how small on-device models let hardware makers ship AI features with no cloud dependency.
picks.rationale: A buildable, Google-authored reference design proving an AI product can ship with zero cloud dependency — the most directly actionable hardware item in the pool.

picks.title: Gemini's revamped Wear OS design is finally rolling out, and it was worth the wait
picks.excerpt: Gemini on Wear OS drops its full-screen app for an overlay that matches the phone experience, with live transcripts and a clearer mic indicator. It is a concrete lesson in adapting assistant UI to a tiny round canvas.
picks.rationale: A shipped, concrete assistant-UI redesign for the smallest canvas — full-screen to overlay, with live transcript and mic-state cues designers can copy tomorrow.

picks.title: Google working on AI-generated lockscreen clocks for Pixel
picks.excerpt: Android Canary 2608 reveals AI-generated lockscreen clocks alongside customizable Quick Settings. Generative UI is moving from wallpapers into functional interface elements on the most-seen screen of the phone.
picks.rationale: Generative UI crossing from decoration into a functional interface element on the most-viewed screen of the phone — a live signal of where system UI design is heading.

picks.title: Kids' smartwatches are meant to keep children safe, but hackers can turn them into stalking devices
picks.excerpt: Researchers used a $30 kids' smartwatch to covertly track location, take photos and record audio, a flaw shared across dozens of GPS watch brands. Always-on sensing wearables are shipping without the security design their form factor demands.
picks.rationale: Hard evidence that always-on sensing wearables ship without the security design their form factor demands — a design-integrity story, not a spec bump.

picks.title: The next age of LLMs? Dev gets a small LLM running at 10 tokens a second locally on a $10 microcontroller
picks.excerpt: A developer ran a 28.9M-parameter model at 10 tokens per second on a sub-$10 microcontroller. If language models fit that budget, almost any connected object becomes a plausible AI interface.
picks.rationale: Redraws the cost floor for embedded AI: at sub-$10 BOM, almost any connected object becomes a plausible conversational interface.
